title: We don't have kids. The baby monitor the last owners left in the attic still picks up someone humming.
story:
We found it the day we moved in, a white monitor on a shelf in the attic, still plugged in, its little green light glowing.

My wife wanted to toss it. I switched on the receiver instead, just to see. Static, and under the static, a soft humming. A lullaby, slow and off-key.

I went up to the attic. Nobody. Just boxes and the monitor. The humming stopped the second I reached the top step.

After that we kept the receiver in the kitchen, mostly as a joke. The humming came most nights around midnight. Then one night it stopped humming and started talking. A woman's voice, very close to the microphone. "Shh. They're awake now. Stay quiet."

I called the woman who sold us the house. I asked if they'd had a baby. She was silent for a long time. Then she said they never had children either. They found that monitor in the attic the day they moved in.

I asked why they left it plugged in.

She said, "Because the one time we unplugged it, she came downstairs to find out why."

That night I sat in the kitchen and watched the receiver. At midnight, the humming started again.

It wasn't coming from the speaker.
premise: abandoned baby monitor in the attic of a childless house picks up a humming woman; she comes down if it is unplugged
